A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPA study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original knowledge-injection experiments on SQuAD, QuALITY and MultiHop-RAG, alongside prompt ablations, diversity measurements and training-framework comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original SPA experiments and adds general-benchmark evaluations of models after knowledge injection in Appendix C.5.

M1.justification: Appendix A revises the documented instruct-model inputs: six templates move generation directives from the user message into the system message, leaving title/context in the user message. The seven strategies, equal-token mixture and training pipeline remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether data were regenerated.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds MMLU, ARC-C, OpenBookQA and WinoGrande to evaluate retained general knowledge and reasoning abilities. This substantially broadens evaluation beyond the three retained knowledge-injection benchmarks; training-corpus coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in corresponding existing experiments is retained. The new general-benchmark evaluations reuse the base models and existing SEAL, EntiGraph and Active Reading comparators without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix C.5 introduces general-benchmark evaluation using lm-eval-harness after 11M SQuAD-based or 455M QuALITY-based training tokens, with replay excluded. Figure 3 also changes some Active Reading token-budget positions. Newly supplied hyperparameters for existing experiments are disclosures, not evidence of changed training settings.

E4.justification: The new catastrophic-forgetting analysis in Appendix C.5 tests whether knowledge injection harms previously acquired capabilities, across four benchmarks and two training regimes. This adds a substantial analysis of potential costs beyond target-task effectiveness. Existing prompt ablations, diversity analyses, framework comparisons and generation examples are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix C specifies diversity-sampling seed 42; v2 Appendix C.4 states only that a fixed seed is used. This removes specific seed information without establishing a changed seed. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests accompany the added results.

E6.justification: Tables 9–10 add general-capability results: SPA averages 61.10 versus base 60.96 after SQuAD training, and 54.33 versus 58.56 after QuALITY training. Table 1 revises Active Reading from 51.13 to 51.75 on QuALITY, and from 79.90 to 83.33 and 78.68 to 84.44 on MultiHop-RAG for Qwen and Llama respectively; SPA scores remain unchanged. Figure 3 replaces Active Reading's scaling curve. Table 4 corrects the Discussions deficit from 5.75 to 3.39 points.

T1.justification: The formal augmentation setup and mathematical content are retained. The token-budget symbol changes, and existing diversity-metric definitions move to Appendix C.4; neither constitutes new mathematical reasoning. No proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a simple seven-prompt baseline, strong scaling performance, diversity collapse in RL-based augmentation, and the competitiveness of carefully designed single-stage prompting.

C2.justification: Appendix C.5 adds an interpretation of capability retention: near-retention after SQuAD training but forgetting after QuALITY training, with SPA described as comparatively less susceptible. It also explains excluding replay to isolate synthetic-data quality and identifies replay as a mitigation. Existing mechanism explanations and applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies MultiHop-RAG's learning-rate search and fixed training settings, discloses linear learning-rate decay for SQuAD and QuALITY, and supplies the exact SQuAD grading prompt. These improve documentation of existing experiments without demonstrating reruns. The code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Five references are added for the four general benchmarks and lm-eval-harness. The discussion of prior knowledge-injection methods and SPA's research positioning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses experimental and diversity descriptions, consolidates appendix material into Training Details and Evaluation Details, updates cross-references, and adds acknowledgements. These are limited editorial and organizational refinements to a largely retained narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–10, relabels Figure 1's learning categories, redraws Figure 3 with adjusted axes, and adds the already-reported full-SPA score to Table 4. Existing tables and figures are also relocated or renumbered, while the overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The added forgetting evaluation addresses a missing practical question, while the training details, grading prompt and Table 4 correction improve reproducibility and clarity. The gains are limited: uncertainty estimates remain absent, the blanket claim of less forgetting exceeds Table 9, where Active Reading has the higher average, and the explicit sampling seed is lost. Overall, v2 offers a useful but bounded improvement.
